title: The actual coefficient-stage identifications respect the normalized shifts
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and an arbitrary scheme $Y$. The universe of $Y$ and the universe of $\Omega$ are independent. Let $I$ be the directed poset of finite coefficient subfields of $\Omega$ [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Use the specified small coefficient models, intrinsic raw rational stages $C_E=D^b_c(Y,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and the datum-free normalized scalar stage system $S$ of [lem-general-algebraically-closed-coefficient-stages]. Write $T_{EL}$ for its transition for $E\le L$, $a_{ELM}:T_{LM}T_{EL}\cong T_{EM}$ for its associator, and $\sigma_{EL,n,K}:T_{EL}(K[n])\cong(T_{EL}K)[n]$ for its fixed integral-image-normalized integer-shift comparison. Let $P=S.\mathrm{PairCategory}$ be the category with literal objects $(E,K)$ and morphisms the classes $[L,u]$ modulo equality after common-stage transport [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. Write $j_E:C_E\to P$ for the specified inclusion. No finite-field datum, geometric base-field structure, noetherian assumption, or Karoubi completion is part of this construction.

Equip $P$ with the uniquely specified shifts and identity-normalized inclusion comparisons $\beta$ of [lem-pur-general-pair-shift-normalization]. For $E\le L$, let
$$\theta_{EL}:j_L T_{EL}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_E$$
be the canonical stage identification [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data], whose component at $K\in C_E$ is represented over $L$ by $a_{ELL,K}:T_{LL}T_{EL}K\to T_{EL}K$. With the composite shift comparison on $j_LT_{EL}$ built from the prescribed $\sigma$ and $\beta$, this actual natural isomorphism commutes with all integer shifts. Explicitly, for every $n\in\mathbf Z$ and $K\in C_E$,
$$
 \beta_{E,n,K}\circ\theta_{EL,K[n]}
 =\theta_{EL,K}[n]\circ\beta_{L,n,T_{EL}K}\circ j_L(\sigma_{EL,n,K}).
$$
Thus its hom natural transformation has $\mathrm{NatTrans.CommShift}$ for $\mathbf Z$ with these already specified comparisons. This includes $E=L$ and repeated finite stages; the comparisons are not replaced by other choices.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-scalar-associator-shifts] to the inclusions $E\le L\le M$. Its auxiliary finite-field datum can have $a=1$ and $p=2$ if $\ell\ne2$, or $p=3$ if $\ell=2$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]; take $k_0=\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z$ and its algebraic closure, which exists by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. This imposes no structure morphism on $Y$. The parameter-independence and normalized-shift identification in [lem-general-algebraically-closed-coefficient-stages] identify its scalar functors and shifts with the prescribed datum-free ones. Its canonical tensor associator is the specified $a_{ELM}$: both are balanced tensor composition followed by the equality of the composite coefficient inclusion with the direct inclusion. Thus its shift equation, with $M=L$, reads
$$\sigma_{EL,n,K}\circ a_{ELL,K[n]}=a_{ELL,K}[n]\circ\sigma_{LL,n,T_{EL}K}\circ T_{LL}(\sigma_{EL,n,K}).$$
The coefficient-inclusion equality is the same on both sides; substituting that equality merely identifies the endpoints. No alternative shift or associator is chosen.

proof.text:
Fix $n\in\mathbf Z$ and $K\in C_E$. By [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data], $\theta_{EL,K}$ has representative $[L,a_{ELL,K}]$ and $j_L(\sigma_{EL,n,K})$ has representative $[L,T_{LL}(\sigma_{EL,n,K})]$. By [lem-pur-general-pair-shift-normalization], the two $\beta$ components in the desired equation are identities on the literal shifted pairs, and
$$\theta_{EL,K}[n]=[L,\sigma_{EL,n,K}^{-1}\circ a_{ELL,K}[n]\circ\sigma_{LL,n,T_{EL}K}].$$
In particular the reflexive transition $T_{LL}$ is retained; it has not been set equal to the identity.

proof.text:
Compose the representatives of Step 2 at their common stage $L$, using [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. The right side of the required square is represented by
$$\sigma_{EL,n,K}^{-1}\circ a_{ELL,K}[n]\circ\sigma_{LL,n,T_{EL}K}\circ T_{LL}(\sigma_{EL,n,K})=a_{ELL,K[n]}.$$
The equality is Step 1 multiplied on the left by $\sigma_{EL,n,K}^{-1}$. The left side, since $\beta_{E,n,K}$ is the identity [lem-pur-general-pair-shift-normalization], has exactly this representative. Equal representatives give equal quotient morphisms. This proves the displayed square.

proof.text: The argument applies to every integer $n$, including $0$ and negative integers, and every $K$. The composite comparison for $j_LT_{EL}$ is precisely $\beta_{L,n,T_{EL}K}\circ j_L(\sigma_{EL,n,K})$ by the definition of the composite shift comparison. Hence Step 3 is the componentwise defining equation for $\mathrm{NatTrans.CommShift}(\theta_{EL}.\mathrm{hom},\mathbf Z)$. It uses no strict inequality of coefficient stages, so also covers $E=L$ and repeated fields.
